prompt: Men's heights are approximately normal with mean $68$ inches and SD $3$ inches. What proportion of men are between $65$ and $74$ inches tall? Give a decimal to three places.
hint: An area between two heights needs two $z$-scores, one for each end of the interval.

hints.text: An area between two heights needs two $z$-scores, one for each end of the interval.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Warm up: between $z = -1$ and $z = 1$ the area is $0.8413 - 0.1587 = 0.6826$. Area between two $z$-values is always "left area of the big one minus left area of the small one."
$65$ is at $z = -1$ and $74$ is at $z = 2$. The table gives $P(Z < 2) = 0.9772$ and $P(Z < -1) = 0.1587$, and the area between is the difference.
$0.9772 - 0.1587 = 0.8185$, so about $0.819$ of men are between $65$ and $74$ inches tall.

explanation: Standardize both ends so the table can be used: $z_1 = \frac{65 - 68}{3} = -1$ and $z_2 = \frac{74 - 68}{3} = 2$.
The table gives areas to the left: $0.9772$ below $z = 2$ and $0.1587$ below $z = -1$.
Subtracting removes the part below $65$ inches: $0.9772 - 0.1587 = 0.8185$, so about $0.819$, or $82$ percent of men.

alternativeExplanations.title: Empirical rule shortcut
steps: From $z = -1$ to $0$ is half of 68 percent: 34 percent.
From $z = 0$ to $2$ is half of 95 percent: 47.5 percent.
Total $34 + 47.5 = 81.5$ percent, close to the table's 81.9 percent (the rule rounds).

alternativeExplanations.title: The trap: adding instead of subtracting
steps: Adding $0.9772 + 0.1587 = 1.136$ is impossible — a proportion cannot exceed 1.
The region between two $z$-values is the big left area with the small left area cut away.
